paper_sections.1-2: Actual reflected-clock process, raw predictable sigma algebra, right-germ martingales and original finite energy integral
paper_sections.3: Exact output measure change and full output-energy product isometry/associativity
paper_sections.4: Separate-energy cross-product integrability, signed joint null quotient, common multiplier bound and actual output identification
paper_sections.5: Target-indexed self-representation, fixed countable family, compact-parameter uniform reconstruction over all causal horizons
paper_sections.6: Original two-source derivative/adjoint, Gaussian fiber recovery and uniform original divergence graph limit

human_reorganization: Proposition 2.1 uses the classical auxiliary martingale regularization/compensator construction and finite-measure uniqueness to identify the same raw measure. The formal source instead proves raw content continuity by compact-fiber approximation; no compensator or pathwise bracket theorem for raw IBM is claimed formalized.

The signed covariance density proof uses polarization and positivity for rational linear combinations, followed by Radon--Nikodym densities. The formal source derives an equivalent variation-density bound from its signed variation Young inequalities.
Uniform convergence is proved directly by a finite compact subcover, equivalent to the formal antitone Dini argument for the net of finite subsets.
The identical-channel example showing failure of unrelated component multipliers is an elementary external deduction, not a separate named formal declaration.

The zero initial projection of each actual process coordinate is reconstructed through clock-conditioned stopped-scenery prediction; the formal proof uses bounded clipped-past factorization and shrinking forecasts.

The joint intrinsic derivative density is an established frozen finite-average-core foundation, mapped via jointDerivative_dense. The paper does not rebuild that core construction or infer differentiability of point observations.

Gaussian source recovery is reconstructed by finite Hermite chaos and closed adjoint graphs, then lifted fiberwise on the two original independent source factors. The retained graph constant three follows from the verified squared-field bound two.

The countable family is chosen by Hilbert-basis existence and target-indexed closed-range representation. It is not an explicit causal-gradient coefficient formula or a predictable representation theorem for a prescribed single martingale.

Section 7 uses the Hilbert norm on the ORIGINAL divergence graph, namely sqrt(||V||^2+||delta V||^2). The generalized derivative f maps a graph test to its L2 pairing with the original divergence value, so its norm is at most ||f|| without native-domain membership.

The fixed tests are the existing bounded linear native recovery applied to the fixed stochastic basis outputs, with norm-squared at most two and exact divergences e_i. Coefficient evaluation, stochastic reconstruction and Parseval are exact source correspondences; the native derivative pairing is stated only for targets in its original domain.

The lower graph-dual norm bound ||f-P0f||/sqrt(3) is an explicitly proved HUMAN deduction: finite combinations of tests, not just individual norm bounds, are controlled by bounded linear recovery and basis orthogonality. The actual point-curve bound and nonzero coefficient at every positive time are human consequences of its exact variance and zero initial projection. No sharpness claim or additional formal declaration is made.

literature.review: Primary full Metivier--Pellaumail 1977 text inspected, especially Sections E/F: general Doleans measures and martingale integration. Classical existence/regularization background credited.

Author full notes inspected, Proposition 5.4, printed p.145: classical continuous-martingale full product-domain associativity. Continuity of the IBM-observable martingales is not assumed from this comparison.

novelty: Classical formalization companion; no new associativity, single-driver predictable representation, temporal Ito/Clark--Ocone, or priority claim.
